topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning outcomes regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine primary, non-targeted approaches that remove tumors physically, damage DNA through radiation, or disrupt cell division using cytotoxic chemical agents.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic signaling dependencies, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe targeted strategies that exploit cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and overcoming drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule kinase inhibitors designed to exploit oncogene addiction and the mechanisms of resistance and drug addiction that arise during treatment.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered antibodies are used either directly to disrupt tumor cell signaling and recruit immune effector functions or to deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Tumor immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for immune surveillance and examine therapeutic interventions that reawaken, redirect, or genetically engineer T cells to target cancer cells.

topics.label: Efficacy trends, genomic stratification, and future challenges in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address broader perspectives in cancer medicine, including genomic matching, historical survival and screening trends, future directions, and ethical dilemmas in clinical care.
